what_the_eye_sees: A smooth gold signet with a big dark-blue dome that reads as an eyeball or a planet, not a sloe, and a row of thin bristles along the shoulder like a fishbone comb or a sea urchin. In the face view it looks like a beetle or a little spaceship: a square boss with one needle sticking out each side and four rivet-like bumps at the corners. The two small domes with white sparks on the cheek read as screws or rivets, not flowers. There is no wood, no bark, no blossom and no branching anywhere, so nothing says plant at all, let alone blackthorn. The walls are plain polished metal and the whole thing reads as mechanical CAD.

changes.where: Cheeks and shank walls, both sides (bark layer, theta roughly 20-160 and 200-340 deg)
changes.change: Make the bark visible: raise relief from 0.35 to the clamp limit (aim 0.5 mm where the bite stays at or under 0.05), with deep furrows running round the ring and lenticel dashes, and darken it with an antique/oxidised recess so the walls read as black knotted wood against the polished rim and spurs. Turn the spurs into twigs: have each long spur spring from a short knuckled side-branch stub (0.8-1.0 mm base, 1.2 mm long) rather than from the bare crest.
changes.acceptance: At 300 px the hero shows rough dark branch texture on every visible wall surface; no wall area reads as smooth polished metal; the shank reads as a thorny black stick.

changes.where: Cheek blossoms (outline::blossom stamps and their 1.3 diamond centres)
changes.change: Grow the blossoms until they are unmistakable five-petal flowers: petal outline diameter from about 2.4 to the cheek's full height minus the 0.3 mm margin (target 3.5-4 mm, use a single larger blossom per cheek if two do not fit), petals 0.5 mm high with distinct notched tips and clear gaps between petals, and add 2-3 smaller 2 mm buds or a second blossom spilling onto the shank wall near theta 45/135. Keep the diamond as the centre but sit it in a stamen ring, not a bare dome.
changes.acceptance: At 300 px a viewer counts five petals on at least one blossom in the hero; the blossoms no longer read as screws or rivets.

changes.where: Shoulder spurs (long and short spur ring patterns, both shoulders) and the sloe seat
changes.change: Fewer, longer, more varied thorns: cut to 4-5 per side, long spurs from 2.6 to 3.5-4 mm with a visible thickened base (base circle 0.5 to 0.7 mm radius) and lean them at clearly different angles so they read as blackthorn spines, not a comb. On the face, break the square boss: give the sloe a bloom-matte onyx (not glossy blue-black sapphire), a small calyx of 5 sepal points under the stone, and a short stalk stub at one end so it reads as a fruit on a twig, not an eye in a socket. Remove or merge the four corner rivet bumps on the face view.
changes.acceptance: Face view at 300 px no longer reads as a spaceship or eye: the stone has a calyx and stalk, and the side needles read as thorns with bases. Hero shows spines of visibly different lengths and angles rather than an even bristle row.
